lenders.name: JPMorgan Chase (Chase Card Services)
lenders.ftype: Personal and business credit cards; business lines of credit and term loans; SBA 7(a) and Express
lenders.min: About 670 for Ink business cards; Freedom Rise accepts no credit history
lenders.notes: Most variable issuer by state. Double pulls (EX plus EQ) are common on new accounts; TransUnion mainly shows up after a Credit Journey prequalification. 5/24 rule; one business card per 30 days. Business cards do not report to personal bureaus. Chase is taking over the Apple Card program from Goldman Sachs.

lenders.name: American Express
lenders.ftype: Personal and business credit cards and charge cards; Business Line of Credit (formerly Kabbage)
lenders.min: About 670 for cards; 660 FICO for the Business Line of Credit
lenders.notes: The most consistent Experian puller (about 95% of 390 datapoints). Limit of 2 credit cards per 90 days; charge cards exempt. Business cards do not report to personal bureaus while in good standing. Credit limit increase of up to 3x can be requested after day 61 on a soft pull.

lenders.name: Citibank (Citi Cards / CBNA)
lenders.ftype: Personal and business credit cards; personal loans; small business lending in branch markets
lenders.notes: Experian about 53%, Equifax about 38%, TransUnion about 9% of 458 datapoints. Double pulls reported for people new to Citi. Forum reports from 2023 say Citi business cards pull Equifax. Sensitive to recent inquiries (trouble reported above 6 in 6 months). Limit of 1 card per 8 days and 2 per 65 days.

lenders.name: Bank of America
lenders.ftype: Personal and business credit cards; unsecured and secured business lines of credit; term loans; equipment loans; secured business card
lenders.min: About 670 for cards; 700 for unsecured business credit
lenders.notes: Experian about 82% of 129 datapoints; TransUnion is the usual fallback and is commonly reported for business cards. 2/3/4 rule on consumer cards; 7/12 with a BofA deposit account. Business cards do not report to personal bureaus. Intro 0% period on Business Advantage cards was cut to 7 billing cycles in January 2026.

lenders.name: Capital One
lenders.ftype: Personal and business credit cards; secured card; business lines and loans
lenders.notes: Pulls all three bureaus on almost every application. Approval can still go through with Experian or Equifax frozen, but not TransUnion for personal cards. Most Spark business cards report to personal bureaus; Spark Cash Plus, Venture X Business and the $95 Venture Business do not. Roughly one new card per 6 months.

lenders.name: Discover (now part of Capital One)
lenders.ftype: Personal credit cards; secured card; personal loans
lenders.min: 660 for personal loans ($25,000 minimum income); secured card for thinner files
lenders.notes: Experian is primary, Equifax second, in the 2023 myFICO grid; some sources name TransUnion. If Experian is frozen you can ask Discover by chat to pull another bureau. Second card only after 12 months; maximum 2 cards. Business card reports to personal. Acquired by Capital One in May 2025.

lenders.name: U.S. Bank

rules: Pull all three reports at annualcreditreport.com and note which bureau is cleanest. Use the Lender Database tab to pick lenders that pull that bureau in your state.

Experian-leaning: Chase, Amex, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, FNBO, PNC, M&T, TD, USAA. TransUnion-leaning: U.S. Bank, Barclays, Synchrony, Navy Federal, Elan, Apple Card. Equifax-leaning: Truist, Citizens, PenFed, DCU, Huntington, KeyBank, Target (TD). All three: Capital One. Applying to one lender from each group keeps any single report from stacking up.

Chase goes first because of 5/24. Then Amex (2 cards per 90 days), then U.S. Bank (dislikes 5+ new accounts in 12 months), then Wells Fargo, then Bank of America, then regionals. Capital One goes last because it hits all three bureaus and most of its business cards report to personal credit.
Use prequalification tools (Capital One, Discover, Amex Apply With Confidence, Upstart, Upgrade, Fundbox, Capital on Tap) to see offers before taking a hard inquiry.
Business credit runs in parallel at every tier
Form the entity, get an EIN and D-U-N-S number, open a business checking account, then add 3 to 5 net-30 vendors. None of this touches personal credit and it supports every later application.
Stated income is still a statement under penalty of law

Low-doc and no-doc mean the lender does not collect tax returns up front. Income and revenue figures must be accurate, and lenders can ask for proof later (Amex financial reviews are the best known example).
Minimum scores are published floors or community estimates. Income, debt-to-income, utilization, account age, recent inquiries and deposits decide the outcome as much as the score.
